author: TEDx Talks
description:
Leaders are taught to control outcomes, manage people, and force change—but control is an illusion. Drawing from two decades of executive leadership, culture transformation research with Stanford Graduate School of Business, and real-world case studies, this talk reframes leadership as an act of surrender. Not surrender as weakness, but as intentional acceptance of reality. 

By letting go of resistance and focusing on the experiences leaders create, organizations build trust, adaptability, and sustained performance. This talk by Dr. Kriegel challenges leaders to move from force to flow—and shows why adaptability is the strongest predictor of long-term success. 

Dr. Jessica Kriegel is a workplace culture expert, keynote speaker, and researcher. As Chief Strategy Officer at Culture Partners, she leads research that challenges outdated ideas about control, power, and performance—offering bold new frameworks that drive real results. She’s the host of the CEO Daily Brief and Culture Lead
title: The power of surrender in leadership | Dr. Jessica Kriegel | TEDxSouthlake

He challenges businesses, innovators, and leaders to move beyond the hype and discover how AI can solve meaningful problems, improve operations, and create lasting impact. Now CEO, he leads a team of 20+ experts driving AI, digital transformation, and software projects with governments and international organizations, while championing a data-driven future in global forums. author: TEDx Talks
description:
In this TEDx talk, Gopichand, a Senior Software Engineer specializing in Large Language Models (LLMs), discusses the role of AI in financial systems. He outlines how AI drives critical daily decisions, such as evaluating loan applications and identifying fraudulent transactions.

He emphasizes that trust in AI should not rely solely on model accuracy. Instead, it must encompass the complete pipeline, including data quality, model monitoring, and rigorous governance. Gopichand introduces a trust architecture consisting of high-quality data, transparent pipelines, monitored models, explainable outcomes, and strong governance, highlighting that human oversight remains vital to keeping financial AI accountable and robust. Gopichand is a Senior Software Engineer, Cloud Data Architect, researcher, and technology leader specializing in Big Data Engineering, Cloud Computing, Artificial Intelligence, and enterprise software systems. He designs scalable data platforms, cloud-native architecture
title: Designing Trustworthy AI in the Financial Landscape | Gopichand  | TEDxVishnu Institute

Architecture is not built, it becomes.

Anthony El Beainy redefines space as a living, evolving experience.

Honest, reflective, and deeply human, her talk resonates with anyone who has ever felt out of sync with expectations, and empowers them to embrace their own pace of growth. author: TEDx Talks
description: Have you ever struggled to say no? Every volunteering opportunity, you’re there. Every club, you join. Every project, your hand is in the air ready to lead. It’s not because you’re genuinely interested and passionate, but rather just because you’re afraid of what might happen if you let go of a potential “life changing decision.” Psychologists have labeled this phenomenon as “Opportunity FOMO”: When you feel the need to say yes to everything to not be left behind or pick the wrong pathway. If you choose one path or take one specific decision, there’s always a possibility of losing a better one, so instead individuals are inclined to say yes to everything. In this talk, Rhea Jhaveri explores this phenomenon and shares her personal experiences with opportunity FOMO. Rhea is a junior at Frisco Heritage High School. She became a TEDx speaker to pursue her passion of speaking to audiences and loves the platform that TEDx provides. The topic of her speech explores the concept of Opportunity

description: We tend to treat neurodegenerative diseases like Parkinson’s and dementia as purely medical conditions, focusing almost entirely on biological treatment. At the same time, loneliness and social isolation are increasing, especially among older adults, and emerging research suggests they are closely linked to cognitive decline. The gap is not a lack of solutions, but how we define the problem itself. To truly support brain health, we need to shift our focus from viewing neurodegeneration as solely a medical challenge to recognizing that human connection is an essential part of prevention and care. author: TEDx Talks
description:
We use the word "psychopath" as a joke all the time, but we rarely ever use it correctly. In this talk, sophomore Paanini Veerubhotla looks at what actually happens when we casually throw this label around, how it affects real people, and how society's words change how we think about ourselves. 

Psychopathy isn't a punchline, it is a real clinical disorder. When we call people psychopaths just for a laugh, they can actually start to internalize it and feel like they fit that mold, which causes a lot of mental strain. By breaking down the neurology and social impact behind these habits, this presentation aims to show the real weight of our words and why accurate understanding matters. Paanini is a sophomore at Frisco Heritage High School. He became a TEDx speaker  to push himself outside his comfort zone and expand on his experience with broadcasting. He wanted to learn how to connect with a live audience and improve his communication in a more real, direct way. Paanini’s speech focus
title: Psychopathy in Society: The Power of the Label | Paanini Veerubhotla | TEDxHeritage HS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
As social media, specifically short-form social media becomes more pervasive in our society, so does the stress of deteriorating mental wellbeing. However, it’s not necessarily easy to connect the two. Instead, the issue might be rooted less in the content that we consume but more in how our minds have subconsciously changed as a result of its consumption.

This presentation by Keerthana Rajasekar delves into what is becoming a very common  practice in today's world: doomscrolling. Starting off as an innocuous habit, scrolling can quickly turn into hours wasted looking at videos and leave us confused as to why we were so easily consumed. Using personal anecdotes, common social media practices, and neuroscientific insights, Keerthana unravels the mystery behind the effects of this habit.

By exploring the ideas behind adaptation and neuroplasticity, Keerthana turns the commonly accepted notion of endless scrolling into a result of poor self-control. She dives into the idea of the brain
title: Addiction vs. Adaptation | Keerthana Rajasekar | TEDxHeritage HS Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description:
Many people grow up being told they are “full of potential” — that they are capable of achieving great things. While this is meant as encouragement, it often turns into an invisible pressure that follows them everywhere. Instead of feeling free to explore, fail, and learn at their own pace, they begin to feel trapped by expectations — both from others and themselves.

This talk explores how the idea of “potential” can quietly become a burden. It affects how we define success, how we handle failure, and how we measure our worth. When people are constantly trying to live up to an ideal version of themselves, they may lose connection with who they truly are in the present moment.

It also reflects on the mental and emotional impact of this pressure, especially among students and young adults who feel they must always be achieving something “big” to prove their value.

Ultimately, this talk asks an important question: what if our worth is not defined by how much potential we have, but by
title: The pressure of being potential | Eilaf Shaikh | TEDxAJ Science College Youth

description:
安斎哲也は議員として町を盛り上げていくことに限界を感じ、農業から人の笑顔を増やすことを目指すことを決意。地域活動や取材、政治への挑戦など、さまざまな経験を重ねる中で実感したのは、一歩踏み出すことで見える景色が変わるということだった。
自身の人生経験をもとに、挑戦することの大切さと、行動が未来を切り拓く力について語る。
できない理由ではなく、できる理由を考える。その小さな意識の変化が、人生を大きく変えるきっかけになるかもしれない。 元 小樽市議会議員
議員として街を盛り上げていくことには限界を感じ、農業から人の笑顔を増やすことを目指している。現在は北海道 藤井ファーム・ラボ株式会社の社員として農業だけでなく、ワカサギ釣り体験など地域資源を生かした観光に力を入れている。 This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: できない→できる理由を考える | 安斎 哲也 (Tetsuya Anzai) | TEDxSapporo Youth

author: TEDx Talks
description: After losing her father, a Peshmerga martyr, at the age of four, Parez grew up facing hardship, uncertainty, and responsibility far beyond her years. In this powerful talk, she shares how resilience, community, and a refusal to adopt a victim mindset helped shape her journey. A moving story of turning loss into strength and challenges into purpose. Only 14 years old, Parez embodies resilience as the daughter of a martyred Peshmerga. With a full scholarship at Cambridge International School, she excels in academics, debates, and international representation, standing as a powerful voice of her generation and a symbol of courage, education, and hope. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: The Power of Not Giving Up | Parez Pasawan | TEDxNishtiman

author: TEDx Talks
description: Marriage is one of the most important relationships in our lives, yet many couples struggle with misunderstandings, communication gaps, and daily challenges. In this talk, Dr. Fazil explores the root causes of marital conflicts and shares practical approaches to building trust, improving communication, and creating stronger, healthier family relationships. A thoughtful conversation on how understanding and connection can lead to a happier marriage and a more stable family life. Dr. Dana Fadhil, PhD in Sociology, is a renowned trainer accredited by international institutions in Canada, the UK, and Lebanon. He has delivered over 20 specialized programs, including the acclaimed 2U Program, empowering more than 10,000 youth and professionals, and sharing his expertise at international conferences. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: What Happy Couples Do Differently? | Dr Dana Fazil | TEDxNishtiman

description: Entrepreneurs do more than build businesses—they create jobs, drive innovation, and strengthen economies. Drawing on global examples and regional realities, Dr Ghaith Mustafa Al-Abdallah explores how small businesses play a vital role in economic growth and resilience. A compelling perspective on why empowering the next generation of entrepreneurs is essential for creating a more prosperous and sustainable future. Dr. Ghaith Al-Abdallah is vice president at Catholic University. He holds a PhD in Marketing and has published over 40 papers in top journals. Before academia, he spent over a decade in marketing and executive management. He also serves as senior fellow of the Higher Education Academy, and acts as external examiner and editorial reviewer for international universities. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
title: Why Economies Need Entrepreneurs? | Dr Ghaith Mustafa | TEDxNishtiman

author: TEDx Talks
description: Many parents and educators ask the same question: What should we do when children don't listen? In this thought-provoking talk, Asuda Soran challenges the traditional belief that a child's role is simply to obey. She explores why constant control, shouting, and expecting immediate compliance may not lead to healthy development. Instead, she invites us to rethink parenting and education through the lens of understanding, growth, and connection. A powerful conversation about raising confident, responsible, and emotionally healthy children in a rapidly changing world. Asuda Soran is a Kurdish educational speaker and trainer based in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq, widely recognized for her advocacy in child development, positive parenting, and youth empowerment. She frequently delivers talks and public seminars on effective communication, educational psychology, and guiding children through modern societal challenges. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but
title: The Art of Understanding Children | Asuda Soran | TEDxNishtiman

description: Technology is shaping the future, but true progress happens when societies move beyond consuming innovation and begin creating it. In this talk, Sinan Majeed explores how robotics and artificial intelligence can serve as a bridge between science, industry, and public policy. By focusing on strong systems, practical skills, and meaningful opportunities, he outlines a vision for building an ecosystem that empowers innovators, supports entrepreneurship, and transforms communities into contributors to the next wave of technological advancement. With two decades of global experience and an MBA from Western Michigan University, Sinan Majeed is a visionary entrepreneur. He co-founded Aljazari Robotics & AI Solutions—the first and one of the largest robotics companies in Iraq—driving innovation, empowering youth, and positioning the country at the forefront of technological progress This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local comm
title: The Next Wave of Innovation | Sinan Majeed | TEDxNishtiman

From the ballet barre to her darkest moment, Faye Morrison traces how the same process that builds a dancer's body — damage, repair, growth — is the exact neurological blueprint for transforming trauma into personal power. Blending the discipline of professional ballet with cutting-edge neuroscience and raw personal experience, she makes the case that every tear, loss, and rupture carries an invitation: not to collapse, but to grow into the most powerful version of yourself. description: Change within the health system is not possible without the buy-in of members of the public. Jane's talk explores how the arts can improve physical and mental health, how engaging in creative activities can help you live longer, and how everybody is an artist. Jane Hearst is the Research and Policy Manager at the National Centre for Creative Health, where she advocates for the role of arts and creativity in healthcare. Her work involves responding to NHS and Government evidence calls and supporting health systems in developing research based  strategies. Jane co-hosts the podcast Creating Mental Wellbeing, based on a creative mental health framework developed during her PhD research. She is also the author and editor of two books on Creative Health and has contributed to a range of short films exploring the impact of creativity on wellbeing.
